oneOf.description:
Check the system clock before the ceremony continues.

Shows the current system time and asks the operator to confirm that it is correct. Place it first, so that every recorded time can be trusted.

Record one person's yes-or-no decision.

Use it for a check that needs human judgment or knowledge of something outside the machine, such as "Verify that every network cable is disconnected".

Compare two values and fail the step if they do not match.

Use it for a check the machine can make on its own, such as comparing a computed SHA-256 digest with an expected one.

Have one person read a value aloud for another to check.

Use it to check a value against something outside the machine, such as a label or a printed document. The value is shown in the NATO phonetic alphabet or in hexadecimal.

Show a value for someone to copy, then remove it from the screen.

The operator reveals the value once and confirms that every row is written down. The transcript records that it was shown, not its value. `rite script` prints a worksheet for the step. A headless run that is not a dry run stops here.

Record which machine runs the ceremony.

Records details such as the hostname, the processor and the operating system as evidence. Place it early in the ceremony.

Ask someone to enter a value and record it as an artifact.

The value is recorded in the transcript. The input format and length fields constrain what can be entered.

Ask someone to enter a secret without recording its value.

The input is hidden, and the secret is erased from memory when the run ends. The transcript records that a secret was entered, not its value. A later step can read it as an input.
Generate a key in a backend.

Encrypt a private key for transport.

Reads `key_to_wrap` and exactly one of `wrapping_key` or `recipient`.

Decrypt a wrapped key and import the recovered key into a backend.

The wrapped data identifies its scheme. The step checks the recovered key against `algorithm` when one is given.

Encrypt data using a key held by a backend.

The backend generates a content-encryption key, encrypts the data with it, and protects it with the step's encryption key. The data itself is not sent to the backend.

Decrypt data encrypted by `encrypt_data`.

The result is a byte artifact available to later steps and erased from memory when the run ends.

Split a secret into shares so that `threshold` of them can recover it.

The step uses the backend for randomness and checks every subset of `threshold` shares before it completes. The shares are stored in one artifact, and later steps can read individual shares.

Recover a secret from shares.

The shares must have the same threshold and length. Shares from different splits can produce an incorrect result without an error, so verify the recovered secret separately. The result is erased from memory when the run ends.

Enter a share from its worksheet.

Each row is checked as it is typed. The step creates a share artifact for later use by `combine_shares`.

Import key material into a backend.

The material can come from a file or an artifact. The action imports the bytes as the key type named by `algorithm`.
Export a keypair's public key as an artifact.

Sign data with a key held by a backend.

The key determines the signature algorithm unless `algorithm` names another one supported by the key.

Verify a signature using the signer's public key.

A backend is optional. Without one, the action verifies in software.
Record a formal statement in the transcript.

Add a participant-supplied random value to the ceremony's entropy.

Later values drawn from the entropy source depend on this contribution.

Record a TPM-signed quote of the device's measurements.

No build of Rite currently supports this action.

Read a certificate from a PIV card.

Reading a certificate from a PIV slot does not require a PIN.

Sign data using a key on a PIV card.

The step asks for the PIN before signing.

Produce a YubiKey attestation for a PIV key.

The YubiKey attestation key in slot F9 signs a certificate for the key in the named slot.

Issue an X.509 certificate for a certificate signing request.

Reads the request and a signing key.

Create a PKCS#10 certificate signing request.

The request is built from `subject` and `san`, then signed with a key held by a backend.

DutyType.description:
What kind of duty is done after the run.

Each kind gives the duty a text for the script, used when it has no `description`. Use `custom` for any other duty, with a `description`.

oneOf.description: Return materials to secure storage.
Give the shares to their custodians.
Give the backup media to its recipients.
Store the ceremony's materials in an archive.
Publish the ceremony record and witness attestations.
Notify stakeholders that the ceremony is complete.
Import the generated keys into the system that uses them.
A duty described in `description`.

format.description: The value's format, such as `hex` or `base64`, or a pattern object such as `{ pattern: "..." }`. If omitted, the value is treated as text. Encoded input is stored as decoded bytes.

message.description: The prompt shown to the person entering the value.

Expression.description: A value given by an expression, known when the step runs.

Format.description: What kind of value a person types.

oneOf.description: Anything the person can type.
Decimal digits only.
ASCII letters and digits.
Bytes as hexadecimal, in either case, two digits per byte.
Bytes as standard base64 with padding.
Bytes as paper32 rows, typed a row at a time from a sheet, a wrong character in a row corrected.
A BIP-39 recovery phrase in the English list, typed a word at a time; the value is its entropy, and a length counts words.

pattern.description: A regular expression the whole value must match.

anyOf.x-message: 'format' must name a format (text, digits, alphanumeric, hex, base64, paper32, bip39) or be { pattern: "..." }

instruction.description: Instructions shown to the participant for producing the random value. Without them, the prompt suggests rolling a die.

san.description: Subject alternative names to include, such as `DNS:example.com` or `IP:192.0.2.1`.

subject.description: The certificate subject, written as an RFC 4514 name such as `CN=example.com,O=Acme,C=US`.

algorithm.description: The algorithm of the key to generate. Defaults to `RSA-4096`.

policy.description: The key's permitted operations and whether it can be exported from the backend. A key used by a later `wrap_key` step must be extractable.

slot.description: A backend-specific location for the key, such as a PIV slot or PKCS#11 slot. The software backend ignores this field.

algorithm.description:
The algorithm of the key the bytes hold.

For an AES algorithm the bytes are the key; for any other they are PKCS#8 DER.

expect_key.description: The expected identity of the key: a `sha256:` fingerprint for a keypair or a `cmac-aes:` check value for a symmetric key. The step fails if the key does not match.

anyOf.errorMessage: 'expect_key' must name the key either as 'sha256:<64 lowercase hex digits>', the fingerprint of a public key, or as 'cmac-aes:<6 lowercase hex digits>', the check value of a symmetric key
anyOf.patternErrorMessage: 'expect_key' must name the key either as 'sha256:<64 lowercase hex digits>', the fingerprint of a public key, or as 'cmac-aes:<6 lowercase hex digits>', the check value of a symmetric key
anyOf.x-message: 'expect_key' must name the key either as 'sha256:<64 lowercase hex digits>', the fingerprint of a public key, or as 'cmac-aes:<6 lowercase hex digits>', the check value of a symmetric key

label.description: The label to assign to the key. Defaults to `imported-key`.

policy.description: The operations the imported key may perform and whether it may be exported from the backend.

issuer_cn.description: The issuer's common name when the step does not read an issuer certificate.

path_len.description: For `sub_ca`, how many CA certificates may follow this one in a chain. Defaults to 0.

profile.description: The certificate profile, which determines its extensions. Defaults to `end_entity`.

validity_days.description: The certificate's validity period in days. Defaults to 3650 days.

KeyPolicyParams.description:
What a key may do, in PKCS#11 terms.

A field left out takes the restrictive choice: the key is persistent, sensitive and not extractable, and its usages are what its algorithm permits, sign and verify for a keypair, wrap and unwrap for an AES key. The key usage in a certificate is a different thing, set by `profile` on `issue_certificate`.

extractable.description: Whether the key may be exported from the backend.

persistent.description: Whether the key remains available after the session ends.

sensitive.description: Whether the backend marks the key as sensitive and prevents plaintext access.

usages.description: The operations the key may perform, such as `sign` or `unwrap`.

wrap_with_trusted_only.description: Whether the key may be wrapped only by a trusted key.

include_cpu.description: Whether to record the processor model. Defaults to `true`.

include_machine_id.description: Whether to record a hash of the machine ID. Defaults to `true`.

include_os.description: Whether to record the operating system and kernel versions. Defaults to `true`.

include_security_features.description: Whether to record the machine's memory protections: RAM encryption, IOMMU DMA protection, and zeroing of freed pages. Defaults to `true`.
